title: Generation of high quality multi-view confocal 3D datasets of zebrafish larval brains suitable for analysis using Virtual Brain Explorer \(ViBE-Z) software
protocol: Prevent pigmentation by incubating living embryos older than one day in egg-water containing 0.2 mM PTU until the desired stage is reached.
Fix larvae at the desired stage in 4% PFA in PBS overnight at 4°C.
Wash larvae five times for 5 minutes each in PBST.
Dehydrate larvae stepwise with increasing concentrations of methanol (5-minute washes: 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% MeOH in PBST).
Store dehydrated larvae in 100% MeOH at -20°C until staining is required.
Rehydrate larvae by washing stepwise with decreasing concentrations of methanol (5-minute washes: 75%, 50%, and 25% MeOH in PBST).
Wash larvae three times for 5 minutes each in PBST.
Determine optimal incubation times for each antigen with proteinase K digestion.
Digest larvae for 30 minutes (for 48 hpf larvae).
Digest larvae for 45 minutes (for 72 hpf larvae).
Digest larvae for 60 minutes (for 96 hpf larvae).
Wash larvae once with PBST after digestion.
Fix larvae again for 20 minutes with 4% PFA ("post-fix").
Rehydrate larvae with stepwise decreasing concentrations of methanol (5 min washing steps each at 75%, 50%, and 25% MeOH in PBST).
Wash larvae 3 times for 5 minutes in PBST.
Bleach larvae for 20 minutes with 1% H₂O₂ in PBST.
Wash larvae 2 times for 5 minutes with PBST.
Digest larvae for 30 minutes (for 48 hpf larvae).
Digest larvae for 45 minutes (for 72 hpf larvae).
Digest larvae for 60 minutes (for 96 hpf larvae).
Wash once with PBST after digestion.
Fix larvae again for 20 minutes with 4% PFA ("post-fix").
Wash larvae 5 times for 5 minutes with PBST.
Pre-hybridize larvae for at least 2 hours in hybridization mix at 65°C.
Hybridize larvae overnight in hybridization mix containing the specific digoxigenin-labeled RNA antisense probe at 65°C.

Wash larvae several times at 65°C: once for 20 minutes in hybridization mix, twice for 20 minutes in 50% formamide in 2x SSCT, once for 20 minutes in 25% formamide in 2x SSCT, and twice for 20 minutes in 2x SSCT.
Wash larvae once for 30 minutes in 0.2x SSCT.
Wash larvae 5 minutes in TNT buffer at room temperature.
Block larvae in TNTB for at least 1 hour.
Incubate larvae overnight with a peroxidase-conjugated anti-digoxigenin antibody at 4°C.
Wash larvae 5 times for 15 minutes with TNT.
Stain larvae according to the TSA kit instructions in the dark for 1 hour.
Wash larvae 3 times for 5 minutes in TNT.
Incubate stained (IHC/FISH) larvae overnight at room temperature in TOTO-3 iodide or SYTOX Green working solution.
Wash larvae 3 times for 5 minutes in PBST.
Transfer larvae to 80% glycerol in PBS and image as soon as possible.
Place larvae in 80% glycerol in PBS for at least six hours.
Melt mounting media in water bath and maintain liquid at 40°C.
Glue two stacks of small cover slips on one large cover slip with cyanoacrylate glue, maintaining about an 8-10 mm distance between the stacks.
Transfer a single larva from an hourglass containing 80% glycerol in PBS to a prepared cover slip using hollow needles.
Remove yolk and cut off the tail of the larva with two hollow needles.
Position the larva into place within the cover slip assembly using hollow needles.
Place a small cover slip (18 x 18 mm) on the spacers.
Confirm that the embryo is not shifted using a dissecting microscope.
Fix the chamber by applying spots of nail polish.
Incubate mounted larva overnight in the dark in a humid chamber at room temperature to let it equilibrate.
Place the cover slip sandwich with the mounted larva into the custom-made aluminum frame.
Fix the cover slip sandwich in the aluminum frame with modeling clay.
Mount the aluminum frame on the microscope stage.
Perform recording of stacks in the first scan position (dorsal anterior part of the head).
Record two stacks at different laser intensities for high dynamic range imaging.
Optimize laser for the first stack such that all signal is in linear range.
Optimize laser for the second stack such that signal deep in the brain is best.
Ensure z-stack depth covers most of the ventral brain.
Perform recording of stacks in the second scan position (dorsal posterior part of the head).
Ensure imaged volume overlaps with the first position by about 20% to enable correct stitching.
Manually turn the sample coverslip sandwich upside-down to record the ventral side.
Perform recording of stacks in the third scan position (ventral anterior part of the head).
Use same laser settings as for the first position.
Perform recording of stacks in the fourth scan position (ventral rostral part of the head).
Use same laser settings as for the first position.
Prepare high dynamic range images by recording each staining, including both specific and nuclear stains.
Adjust two intensities per side (dorsal and ventral) and part (frontal and rostral).
Set low intensity first to minimize bleaching without overexposure.
Ensure deep brain structures are visible at high intensity despite surface structure overexposure.
Maintain microscope settings: Zeiss LSM510-i-NLO laser scanning confocal microscope, LD LCI Plan-Apo 25x/0.8 Imm Korr multi immersion objective.
Acquire stacks at 512x512 pixels resolution with 1 cubic micrometer voxel size.
Use zoom factor of 0.7 and glycerol as the immersion medium setting.
Operate in 12-bit mode, multi track scan mode.
Apply appropriate lasers, filters, excitation, and emission wavelengths as specified.
Import recorded stacks into ImageJ using the import plugin suitable for the confocal microscope brand type software.
Install the HDF5 data format plugin in ImageJ.
Save stacks in HDF5 format.
Create an account at "http://vibez.informatik.uni-freiburg.de/".
Upload files to the website.
Follow instructions for processing provided on the site.
